gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Xbox consoles ignore a generic USB microphone. Maono's own support page says the Xbox 'deliberately does not support' the USB Audio Class standard and is built around the controller's 3.5 mm jack. So on Xbox the only wired option is a 3.5 mm headset (EKSA's E900 Pro manual: 3.5 mm cable into the newer controller), and ChatGPT's advice to 'buy a standalone mic instead' fails there.
standout_why: ChatGPT ran no search and got no results, so no cited rival page exists to compare against. Its answer rates a standalone mic 'Great' for gaming communication and tells people who already own headphones to buy a standalone USB mic. It gives no platform caveat, and on Xbox that advice gives the user a mic the console ignores. None of its answer's text covers console compatibility (PS5 USB/3.5 mm, Xbox 3.5 mm only, Xbox 360 excluded, 7.1 surround only on Windows).
decides: It splits the pick by console. Xbox players should get a headset (3.5 mm into the controller, or an Xbox-licensed wireless model) because a USB desk mic like the Maono PD200X/PD200XS or FIFINE AM8 will not be recognised. PC, Mac and PS5 players can choose either. A standalone USB mic only makes sense on PC/Mac/PS5, and the XLR route needs a separate interface or mixer.

findings.label: Xbox and generic USB microphones
findings.value: Not supported: Xbox 'deliberately does not support' the USB Audio Class standard. A standard USB mic lacks the 'Designed for Xbox' authentication chip, so 'the Xbox sees an unauthorized device and simply ignores it.'
findings.source_title: Why Your USB Microphone Doesn't Work on Xbox (And Why It's Not Your Fault) – Maono FAQ
findings.note: Maker support document, last modified 2025-11-07. It names no Maono model, so it applies to all of Maono's USB mics in principle. It offers no USB workaround.

findings.label: Xbox wired headset path
findings.value: Controller 3.5 mm jack: 'The controller then wirelessly (or wired) transmits all audio to and from the console.'
findings.source_title: Why Your USB Microphone Doesn't Work on Xbox (And Why It's Not Your Fault) – Maono FAQ
findings.note: The page names Turtle Beach, Razer and SteelSeries as makers that license 'Designed for Xbox' headsets.

findings.label: Supported connections
findings.value: USB-C: computers, smartphones, tablets (Android may need OTG enabled; iPhone 15 and later connect directly; iPhone 14 and earlier need a Lightning-to-USB adapter). XLR: 'works only with an audio interface (or mixer)'. No 48 V phantom power needed. No console listed.
findings.note: Last modified 2026-10-26. This is the PD200X FAQ. The PD200XS on our page is the same mic sold with a boom arm, but this page doesn't name it. The FAQ doesn't mention PS4, PS5, Xbox or Switch.

findings.label: XLR-mode limitation
findings.value: In XLR mode the onboard knobs and indicator light are disabled: 'volume adjustment and level monitoring are handled by the external device'.
findings.note: The FAQ calls unresponsive buttons and a dark light in XLR mode normal.

findings.label: PS4 / PS5
findings.value: 'Connect your PS4/PS5 directly using the USB or 3.5 mm audio cable'; the mic is set up in the console's audio settings.
findings.source_title: EKSA E900 Pro 2-in-1 Gaming Headset Manual (ManualsLib)
findings.note: Copy of the maker's manual hosted on ManualsLib. EKSA's own page returned HTTP 429.

findings.label: Xbox
findings.value: Xbox One S/X: plug the 3.5 mm cable straight into the newer controller's jack. Original Xbox One: 'needs a Microsoft adapter (not included)'. Xbox 360: 'not compatible'.
findings.source_title: EKSA E900 Pro 2-in-1 Gaming Headset Manual (ManualsLib)
findings.note: The manual doesn't name Xbox Series X|S. Series X|S controllers keep the same 3.5 mm jack, but the manual doesn't say so.

findings.label: 7.1 surround
findings.value: Needs the USB cable, and 'EKSA Surround 7.1 driver only supports Windows system'. Consoles and Mac get stereo only.
findings.source_title: EKSA E900 Pro 2-in-1 Gaming Headset Manual (ManualsLib)
findings.note: Our page calls it a '7.1' headset; this is the manufacturer's limit on that feature.

findings.label: Which Arctis work on Xbox Series X|S vs PS5
findings.value: Xbox list: Arctis 1 and Arctis 3 Console (3.5 mm to the controller), Arctis 1 Wireless for Xbox (USB, 'Designed and licensed for Xbox'), Arctis 9X (Xbox Wireless). USB-only models (Arctis 5, 7, 7P, 9, Pro, Pro Wireless) appear only in the PS5 list.
findings.source_title: All Arctis headset compatibility with PlayStation 5 / Xbox Series X / Xbox Series S? – SteelSeries Support
findings.note: Shows the same rule from a headset maker: on Xbox, USB audio works only on licensed models; on PS5, plain USB works. The page has no date and no statement on the Nova series.
